minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board met solely to finalize the town's legislative earmark requests for the FY27 state budget, working from capital plan items and a superintendent request for school security upgrades. After discussing and pricing options including fire department radios, a primary school playground design, public safety building boiler upgrades, Fitzgerald field improvements, and Turkey Hill/primary intercom and middle-high school radio upgrades, the board dropped two items to comply with a one-to-three project guideline and voted by roll call to approve a final prioritized list of boiler upgrades, fire department radios, and the primary school playground design, to be sent to the legislative delegation.

what_happened.line: Select Board voted by roll call to submit a three-item FY27 state earmark list: boiler upgrades, fire radios, primary school playground design.
The board dropped a bundled intercom/radio security request and the Fitzgerald field project after learning state guidance caps towns at one to three earmark requests.
Board ranked public safety building boiler upgrades as the top priority, ahead of fire department radios and the playground design.
The town manager will add justifications to the earmark letter and send it to all three members of the legislative delegation, not just one representative.
A separate Flat Hill supplemental budget request is being pursued by the delegation outside this earmark list.

why_it_matters: An earmark is a request for state funding outside the town's own budget, so dropping the school intercom and middle-high radio security upgrades from this list means that project now has to compete for town capital dollars instead.
The ranked order signals which project the delegation will push hardest for as the state budget moves through the legislature this session.
This affects the public safety building, the fire department, and the primary school -- not this year's town tax bill, since these are requests to the state, not town appropriations.
